title: Tight margin sprint buffer & bid-price probe (May 2026)
content:
Purpose:
- Quick working sheet to validate how a 8-12% downward drift in per-token bid price + a short, high-volume sprint (4–6 weeks) affects run-rate runway and hiring triggers. This is intentionally lightweight: meant for an exec-ready one-pager after decisions.

High-level summary / headline thinking (TL;DR):
- If spot bid price / take-rate compresses by ~10% and QPS spikes +50% for 6 weeks, we need a 6–8 headcount rotation buffer (mixed infra + ops) to keep latency targets while preserving a 4pp margin buffer.
- Short-term levers: temporary contract GPU hours, tighter batching + aggressive KV cache TTL, selective model quantization for non-latency-critical routes.
- Hiring triggers: only hire full-time if 6-week moving average of token spend > $1.1M/month or sustained latency SLO violations > 2% for 3 weeks.

Assumptions (working):
- Baseline token mix: 70% chat gen (1.2k tokens req avg), 20% embeddings, 10% rerank.
- Baseline gen price (rev) per 1k tokens: $0.60; baseline cost per 1k tokens executed (infrastructure + ops amortized): $0.22.
- Current blended gross margin: ~63%.
- Sprint shock profile: +50% QPS for 6 weeks; token mix shifts to 80% gen.
- Price compression scenario A: -8% realized rev per token; scenario B: -12% rev; scenario C: -18% (extreme).
- Short-term cost mitigation: batching improvements reduce cost/token by up to 6% (opt-in), KV caching reduces repeated prefix cost by 4% for eligible routes.

Scenario matrix (summary numbers, monthlyized view):
- Base (no shock): Revenue $2.8M, Cost $1.0M, Gross margin 64%, Runway effect: nominal.
- Shock A (-8% price, +50% QPS for 6w, partial batching): Revenue $2.6M, Cost $1.38M, Gross margin 47%, Extra burn vs plan: $380k / month during sprint.
- Shock B (-12% price, +50% QPS for 6w, partial batching + caching): Revenue $2.46M, Cost $1.34M, Gross margin 45.5%, Extra burn: $320k / month.
- Shock C (-18% price, +50% QPS, limited mitigation available): Revenue $2.3M, Cost $1.46M, Gross margin 36.5%, Extra burn: $460k / month.

Headcount / resourcing recommendations (mix & phasing):
- Immediate (weeks 0–4 of sprint): +2 contractors (GPU ops / infra provisioning) to stand up burst capacity and run quantized variants; +1 SRE on-call rotation for latency ops; +1 SolutionsEng for high-touch customers (CS churn risk).
- Short buffer (weeks 4–8): +3 flexible FTE (2 infra / 1 product ops) to stabilize rollouts if sprint persists beyond 6 weeks. Convert contractors to FTE only if 6-week moving average burn delta > $300k/month.
- Long-term hire rule: convert to FTE if sustained price compression > 6 months and model/quantization roadmap requires dedicated infra owners.

Hiring triggers (explicit thresholds):
- Trigger H1 (convert contractor -> FTE): moving avg extra spend >= $300k/mo for 6 weeks AND expected persistent uplift in QPS (sales signals + product roadmap).
- Trigger H2 (immediate full-time hire ramp): latency SLO breach >2% for 3 consecutive weeks AND effort to resolve requires >3x contractor hours/week.
- Trigger H3 (no hire, cost route): revoke burst capacity and implement throttles if customer churn risk < 4% and sales confirms ability to pass temporary credits.

Operational playbook (short checklist):
- Day 0: enable burst pool, tag heavy routes, flip quantized fallback policy for non-critical models.
- Day 3: enable aggressive batching config on low-latency-tolerant routes, TTL 10s for KV cache on multi-turn flows.
- Day 7: monitor per-route margin, per-token cost, and top-20 customer usage; run daily burn delta report.
- Week 2: reconvene with sales/CS to review top-10 customers for credit pass-through or throttling.

Quick sensitivity table (one-liners):
- 1% rev compression ~ $28k/month revenue loss at baseline scale.
- 1% cost reduction via batching ~ $10k/month savings.
- Converting 1 contractor -> FTE adds ~$12k/month opex (fully loaded).

Open questions / unknowns:
- Real elasticity: how much demand actually drops when we nudge price? Need a quick A/B on small cohort.
- Customer credit policy: do we have authority to offer temporary credits > $50k without CS leadership sign-off?
- Technical debt: how many routes will regresses after quantization? We should tag a fallback path.

Concrete TODOs (owner assignments):
- Aisha: run a quick token-elasticity A/B on 5 mid-market customers (deadline: 2026-05-18).
- Ravi: estimate contractor sourcing timeline and 6-week cost (deadline: 2026-05-14).
- Hannah: prepare executive one-pager with top-line numbers + decision tree for Friday review (deadline: 2026-06-04).

Appendix (detailed working rows - copy into spreadsheet):
- Row format: scenario | rev | cost | margin | extra burn | contractor-FTE-mix | notes
- Base | 2,800,000 | 1,000,000 | 64% | 0 | none | nominal
- Shock A (-8%) | 2,576,000 | 1,380,000 | 47% | 380,000 | 2c + 1sre | partial mitigation
- Shock B (-12%) | 2,464,000 | 1,344,000 | 45.5% | 320,000 | 2c + 1sre + 1se | caching benefits
- Shock C (-18%) | 2,296,000 | 1,456,000 | 36.5% | 460,000 | 3c + 2fTE | extreme compression

Notes to self (informal):
- Keep this in drive as working artifact; spreadsheet tab will host full month-by-month phasing.
- This doc is intentionally conservative on mitigation; ops historically overestimates batching gains.
- Walk through these numbers with product-hosted-api and serving-runtime leads before pitching to execs.

End of sheet.
